messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 latency SLO breach detected for /v1/stream endpoint in eu-west-1 - current p99=5.2s (SLO=2.0s). paging eng-oncall.
carol (eng-oncall): on it. any customer hits visible?
ops-bot: routing: impacted tenants: tenant-ark, tenant-ivy (streaming). error-rate steady, only latency spike.
sam (eng-runtime): seeing big tail in continuous-batching path. p50~200ms p95~1.1s p99~5s. spike correlates with high mix of seq-lens — lots of 1-8 token requests queued with a few 2048 token requests.
neha (eng-sre): can you dump current batcher state? which scheduler is used (fairshare vs latency-first)?
sam (eng-runtime): dumping now, attaching snippet: ```json
{"queue_len": 17, "avg_batch_size": 32, "long_tasks_in_front": 2, "scheduler": "latency_first_v2"}
```
carol (eng-oncall): latency_first_v2 will prefer packing long requests — that explains short requests waiting behind long KV cache fills. streaming clients hold open connections while waiting for first tokens -> stalls.
dmitri (product): we have a customer support ticket open from tenant-ark reporting streaming timeouts, started ~10m ago. SLA risk.
neha (eng-sre): mitigation suggestion: 1) enable preemptive scheduling fairness to avoid long requests blocking short ones, 2) cap max_batch_size for streaming route to 8, 3) create a redirect for streaming traffic to a lower-latency dedicated pool if available.
sam (eng-runtime): agree. quick changes: set `batcher.max_batch_ms=8` and `batcher.max_batch_size=12` for /v1/stream; toggle `scheduler.preemptive_fairness=true`. Applying now in eu-west-1 canary.
carol (eng-oncall): also reduce `kv_prefetch` for long requests to avoid blocking CPU during first token.
sam (eng-runtime): running rollout: ```bash
# canary config patch
curl -X PATCH https://deploy/api/configs/batcher --data '{"route":"/v1/stream","max_batch_ms":8,"max_batch_size":12,"preemptive_fairness":true}'
```
sam (eng-runtime): applied to 3 nodes (canary). verifying metrics.
(neha reacts with :hourglass_flowing_sand:)
sam (eng-runtime): p99 on canary dropped to 0.9s within 30s. open nodes 0/3 showing backlog. pushing to remaining nodes with rolling restart of batcher.
dmitri (product): notify tenant-ark support that we're rolling a fix and asking them to test streaming again.
carol (eng-oncall): sam — do we have telemetry to show affected percentage of requests that hit cont-batch vs streaming-batcher? need to quantify customer impact for postmortem.
sam (eng-runtime): yes, attaching quick stat: cont-batch traffic for /v1/stream was ~42% of total tokens in eu-west-1 during spike. affected requests (short seq) saw 40-60x queuing behind long seq.
neha (eng-sre): also see elevated memory pressure on those canary nodes from KV cache thrash. increased evictions. added a temp limit `kv_cache.max_items=50` for canary to keep footprint down.
carol (eng-oncall): good. keep monitoring. status?
sam (eng-runtime): rollout finished at 1767001600. eu-west-1 p99 now 1.0s, p95 350ms. p99 previously 5.2s -> now within SLO. no errors observed.
dmitri (product): tenant-ark confirms streaming improved, will validate load test.
neha (eng-sre): creating a short incident ticket with timeline and mitigation steps. assign to sam for follow-up runtime fix and to carol for handoff notes.
carol (eng-oncall): handwritten mitigation summary for postmortem: 
- root cause: continuous-batching scheduler (latency_first_v2) allowed long seqs to dominate batches, causing short/streaming requests to wait for large KV cache operations -> streaming stalls and p99 spike
- immediate mitigations: enabled `preemptive_fairness`, tightened `max_batch_ms` and `max_batch_size` for /v1/stream route, temporary KV cache limit, rolled changes to all nodes in eu-west-1
- customer impact: tenant-ark and tenant-ivy experienced increased streaming TTF first token time and transient timeouts during 10:12-10:18 UTC; no data loss, some requests retried by clients
- next actions: (a) implement scheduler change to detect mixed-seq workloads and create short-request fast-lane, (b) add configurable route-level defaults for streaming with stricter batch caps, (c) add alerts for mixed-seq imbalance and KV eviction spikes.
carol (eng-oncall): handing off to next oncall @neha. include link to incident ticket and the canary config diff.
neha (eng-sre): acknowledged — I'm on for the next 8h. I'll monitor eu-west-1 and keep the ticket updated.
sam (eng-runtime): will open an RFC for scheduler fairness changes and include perf sims. cc @dmitri for product priority.
dmitri (product): please include customer impact numbers and suggested timeline for a stable fix. ops will want a config guardrail in the console.
carol (eng-oncall): closing on-call thread. will mark as mitigated and schedule postmortem for tomorrow 11:00 UTC. thanks all :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: INCIDENT-MITIGATED: p99 SLO exceeded resolved. ticket #INC-2026-482 created.
